By Abiral Pokhrel

Staff correspondent — and the entire staff

Butwal, Nepal — I’m Abiral. I study Computer Systems Engineering at ISMT College Butwal (University of Sunderland) — graduating June 2028. My real classroom is GitHub: everything I build is open to inspect.

Messy data in, clean answers out. That’s the work I love. When my group left our enterprise project, I finished it solo. I ship, I document, I move on to the next build.

Now: a remote data engineering internship. Bring me a real pipeline — I’ll bring the hands that finish it.

Serverless — AWS

ghtrends: The World’s Code, Read Hourly

A serverless pipeline that listens to GitHub around the clock and reports back on what the world is building.

Hourly ingestServerless AWSTop 500 searchable

Every hour it ingests the GitHub Archive — stars and pull requests — and lands Parquet in S3.

Glue catalogues it. dbt models it into a daily trends table. Streamlit shows it — searchable by meaning, not just by name. No server stays awake all night.

Agents — The Bucker Doctrine

Intelligence, I Argue, Is in the System

Bucker is a free agentic coding harness built on a heresy: that the best result comes not from the dearest model, but from the best system around a free one.

Free models onlyv2.0.0 installerCI green

Most agents rent brilliance from a frontier model. Bucker bets the opposite: build the harness well, and a free model goes further than you’d expect.

Judged by one question — how weak a model can still succeed inside it? One honest smoke test left before v2.0.0 drops its pre-release label. Printed here, not hidden.
